hints: Focus on what fizzing with sodium carbonate tells you about the functional group present in T.
Remember that carboxylic acids fizz to give CO2, while aldehydes and esters do not, so statement 3 can be decided straight away.
Calculate % by mass of O as (mass of O in formula / Mr) x 100 for propanal and ethyl butanoate to see which fit 27.6%.
walkthrough:
**Use the carbonate test to rule out acids**

Carboxylic acids react with aqueous sodium carbonate to give CO2 gas, which is seen as fizzing.

$$\text{RCOOH + Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{RCOONa + CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Aldehydes and esters do not react, so no fizz is seen.

**Apply this to statements 1, 2 and 3**

Statement 3, 3-methylpentanoic acid, is a carboxylic acid so it would fizz. It cannot be T.
Statement 1, propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$), is an aldehyde and statement 2, ethyl butanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$), is an ester. Both would show no fizz, so both are still possible.

**Check the 27.6% oxygen data**

For propanal, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$:
$$M_r = (3 \times 12) + (6 \times 1) + 16 = 58$$
$$\% \text{O} = \frac{16}{58} \times 100 = 27.6\%$$
This fits perfectly.

**Check the ester and the acid**

For ethyl butanoate, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$:
$$M_r = (6 \times 12) + (12 \times 1) + (2 \times 16) = 116$$
$$\% \text{O} = \frac{32}{116} \times 100 = 27.6\%$$
This also fits. 3-methylpentanoic acid is also $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$, so it also has 27.6% O, but it was already ruled out by the fizz test.
Therefore 1 and 2 only are possible.

options.A: Incorrect because although all three compounds contain 27.6% O by mass, statement 3 is a carboxylic acid and would fizz with sodium carbonate to release CO2. T shows no fizz, so 3 must be excluded.
options.B: Correct because 1 and 2 both show no fizz and both fit the percentage. Propanal has Mr 58 with one O giving 27.6% O, and ethyl butanoate has Mr 116 with two O giving 27.6% O.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statement 3. 3-methylpentanoic acid does have the correct % O (Mr 116, 32/116 x 100 = 27.6%), but as an acid it would fizz with carbonate, so it cannot be T.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only statement 1. Propanal alone is not the full answer, as ethyl butanoate also has no fizz and also has 27.6% O by mass, so statement 2 must also be included.
